materials.name: glass-shell
materials.value: ShaderMaterial; transparent:true; depthWrite:false; FrontSide; base alpha:.012; Fresnel exponent:3.2; curve exponent:1.6; alpha capped at .8
materials.purpose: Thin transparent lathed shell and cloned torus-rim material. Bundled studio-small-09.hdr supplies directional reflection, with stronger edges and a narrow pane highlight; no physical refraction.

materials.name: studio-reflection
materials.value: HDRLoader; direct equirectangular shader sample; PMREM world.environment; environmentIntensity:.5
materials.purpose: Bundled real HDR reflection for the glass; the shader retains its edge tint and pane highlight if the image cannot load.

materials.name: cork
materials.value: CanvasTexture base:#bd9567; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xffffff; bumpScale:.028; roughness:.96; envMapIntensity:.18
materials.purpose: Procedurally textured stopper and small top bevel.

materials.name: pixel-sand-field
materials.value: CPU grainField; seeded LCG:907; sample interval:1.9px; jitter:1.7px; 85% 2×2 grains, otherwise 1×1; NearestFilter; generateMipmaps:false
materials.purpose: Loose play only. Hard pixel grains carry image-derived color, per-grain shade variation and a brighter top-left pixel over seeded dark gaps. The user-provided cat grain reference guides this treatment.

materials.name: loose-photo-plane
materials.value: CanvasTexture; MeshBasicMaterial toneMapped:false; PlaneGeometry:5.7×3.42; canvas width=clamp(round(min(stageWidth*.9,stageHeight*1.36)*1.2),240,720); height=round(width*.6)
materials.purpose: Visible loose photograph field; pointer dragging updates CPU grain positions and repaints the texture.

materials.name: photo-mantle
materials.value: 1536×~920 color and tangent-normal CanvasTextures; seeded LCG:173; irregular hull sides:5–7; tilted crown and bevel faces; grain pitch:8.6px; local-color base:.76; contact-shadow color:.43, coverage:.34, offset:(.65,.85), blur:.6; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xbebebe; normalScale:(.9,.9); roughness:.94; metalness:0; envMapIntensity:.14; map and normalMap wrapS:RepeatWrapping, anisotropy:4; no bumpMap; material dispose owns normalMap.dispose; LatheGeometry radial segments:160; maximum radius:.966; y:-1.535 to 2.10; rotationY:PI
materials.purpose: Opaque packed sand follows the inner glass through shoulder and neck and receives lighting and shadows. Height-based UVs contain the photo once in the straight band from y=-1.49 to 1.20, preserving proportions against the actual circumference and height. Sand-colored support fills the remaining surface. Seam width is applied before the grain color and normal atlases. Rasterized hull, crown and bevel faces define grain color and normals without per-grain mesh geometry or grain collisions.

materials.name: packed-sand-cap
materials.value: 256×256 color and tangent-normal CanvasTextures over #bda17a; seeded LCG:173; irregular hull sides:5–7; tilted crown and bevel faces; grain pitch:4.4px; local-color base:.76; contact-shadow color:.43, coverage:.34, offset:(.65,.85), blur:.6; MeshStandardMaterial color:0xbebebe; normalScale:(.9,.9); roughness:.94; metalness:0; envMapIntensity:.14; map and normalMap wrapS:RepeatWrapping, anisotropy:4; no bumpMap; material dispose owns normalMap.dispose; CircleGeometry radius:1; rotationX:-PI/2; scaled by sandRadiusAt(level)
materials.purpose: A sand-colored top cap matches the packed body material, with the same rasterized grain color and crown and bevel normals at a smaller texture pitch. It follows the clipping plane during assembly and rests at y=2.10 in the sealed state. The opaque body and cap form the sand volume without a separate dark core. The cap has no per-grain mesh geometry or grain collisions.

materials.name: assembly-grains
materials.value: 2500 ShaderMaterial Points; transparent:false; depthWrite:true; point size clamped:1–4px; top-left highlight:.045
materials.purpose: Temporary flying grains visible from 8% to 97% of assembly progress; hidden in both settled loose and sealed presentations.

materials.name: plinth
materials.purpose: Low cylindrical display base and shadow receiver.

camera.name: stage-fit
camera.value: PerspectiveCamera fov:32; sealedDistance=max(9.4,8.5/aspect); looseDistance=max(9.4,1.5+11.03/aspect); loose elevation:.094; sealed elevation:.45

narrative.northStar: A personal display plinth in warm daylight
narrative.overview:
A quiet personal display plinth in warm daylight is the implementation’s working visual metaphor. Warm paper, brown ink and restrained terracotta controls frame the photograph as a small object to keep. The photograph supplies the vivid color; the surrounding interface stays low in chroma.

This system is extracted from the rebuilt application. The user-provided cat grain reference guides loose play. The Smithsonian and Petra photographs recorded in [Visual references](docs/visual-references.md) guide the dense packed sand, filled profile and perspective. The interface and bottle remain a code-led interpretation. The user rejected the earlier smoother sand, selected B's independent irregular grains, then requested stronger grain depth. The current crown and bevel normals follow that direction. B is the selected direction, not acceptance of the current strength or the full bottle. The name 砂藏 / Sandkeep remains provisional. Reflective glass, textured cork, faceted packed sand and a contact shadow describe the current rendering choices without claiming photorealism.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, low-chroma interface around a colorful personal photograph.
Chinese serif display type paired with Chinese system sans controls.
A large object stage with compact controls and visibly separated states.
Restrained interface depth; material depth is concentrated in the 3D object.

rules.name: The Photograph Color Rule
rules.body: Let the photograph supply the vivid color. Use clay for the principal action, focus and small identity accents.

rules.name: The Two Type Voices Rule
rules.body: Use the bundled serif for the product name and main headline; use the system sans stack for controls and supporting copy.

rules.name: The Object Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep interface surfaces flat; express material depth through the bottle, cork, grains, plinth and scene contact shadow.

dos: Do use the existing paper, ink, muted, line, clay and stage roles instead of introducing parallel surface colors.
Do preserve the bundled serif headline and system sans control relationship.
Do keep interactive targets at least the observed 44px height or diameter, with the existing clay focus treatment.
Do place the object before creation controls when the studio becomes one column.
Do preserve the finished photograph while turning the bottle and respect reduced motion.
donts: Don't add card shadows or rounded floating panels to the currently flat interface.
Don't use the scene’s photo colors as competing interface accents.
Don't blur the loose field's hard pixel grains, top-left highlights or dark gaps.
Don't copy the loose field's dark gaps onto packed sand. Keep packed grain variation near its local photo color.
Don't treat the loose-grain reference or real-bottle photographs as user approval of the full bottle.
